messages:
dinesh: sec-bot alerted on anomalous use of a host-api key — outbound requests from an IP we don't recognize. seen ~11:42 UTC.
sec-bot: [automated] high-error/high-volume API key usage detected: key_id=ak_live_03de***, unusual ip=88.212.45.19, endpoints(/v1/generate,/v1/embeddings), rate=1k/min, geo=EU.
oncall-sre: tagging as incident, starting containment checklist.
alice: +1. can we confirm whether this is a hosted key or a customer-managed token?
dinesh: looks like a hosted API key (created by portal user: infra-service-account). key metadata shows created 2025-11-02. used in production region eu-west-1.
ben-platform: grabbing audit logs now. run: `rg "ak_live_03de" /var/log/redwood/audit/* | tail -n 200`
ben-platform: results: 320 lines since 11:30, mostly /v1/generate calls with small prompt sizes but sustained. sample IPs: 88.212.45.19, 88.212.45.21. user-agent shows curl/7.86.
carol-cs: any customer reports of anomalous behavior (billing spikes, odd outputs)?
alice: checking billing and tenant mappings to that key_id. key maps to internal ingestion pipeline, not a customer tenant. risk = data exfil from internal pipeline.
ben-platform: confirmed no direct customer API keys tied. but ingress pipeline has had data from multiple customers queued before processing. need to assume potential data exposure until proven otherwise.
oncall-sre: immediate actions: 1) rotate/invalidate key, 2) snapshot and preserve audit logs, 3) throttle/blacklist IPs, 4) notify incident response channel and legal.
dinesh: prepared rotation command, will create replacement key and add temporary block for old key: `redwood-cli keys rotate --id ak_live_03de --create-new --preserve-mapping`
alice: wait — don't rotate without snapshotting KV and logs; if attacker is using key for live requests we want to capture headers and bodies for triage. ben-platform, preserve logs and instrument a debug mirror to capture full request metadata for the next 60s.
ben-platform: starting capture now, piping to secure bucket s3://incidents/1749304567/ — `aws s3 cp --recursive /tmp/capture-174930 .` will preserve and lock retention.
carol-cs: I'm opening an internal CS note in case customers need heads-up. recommend holding public comms until we understand scope.
oncall-sre: blocking IPs at the network edge: firewall rules pushed to edge-proxy cluster — `edgectl ban 88.212.45.19/32` (done). monitoring for other IPs from same ASN.
dinesh: rotated the key at 11:52 UTC and marked old key as revoked/expired. new key created ak_live_rot_1749. rotation command output: 
```
> redwood-cli keys rotate --id ak_live_03de --create-new --force
rotating key... done
old_key_state: revoked
new_key_id: ak_live_rot_1749
```
ben-platform: captured ~90s of traffic before block. saved raw requests and request bodies to the incident bucket.
alice: can infra confirm no other keys were reused or similar patterns? run detection across keys for last 24h for same IPs/UA.
ben-platform: running correlator: `python tools/correlate_ips.py --ips 88.212.45.19,88.212.45.21 --hours 24` -> found 6 keys touched, all belong to ingestion services; no customer keys.
carol-cs: legal asked whether PII might have been in payloads. ben, can you grep payloads for email addresses, ssn patterns, or base64 attachments?
ben-platform: grep outputs: found 14 payloads containing email-like regexes and 2 payloads with long base64 blobs (possible attachments). moving those to high-priority review.
oncall-sre: severity update: P2 until we confirm extent of customer data in those payloads.
dinesh: next steps: - preserve evidence and lock retention - run content scan (pii/hashes) - rotate/expire all ingestion pipeline keys and replace with short-lived tokens + RBAC tighten - alert legal + customer success for targeted outreach if we find customer data - add IDS rule for similar UA/IP combos
alice: I will schedule a short post-incident review: focus on RBAC for service accounts and audit log retention policy. also check KMS key access patterns — ensure HSM logs enabled for rotation.
ben-platform: note: KMS logs show decrypt requests matching timeframe from `svc-ingest-prod` role. will open IAM ticket to remove that role's long-lived credentials and replace with instance role/short-lived STS.
carol-cs: draft comms ready as private note to stakeholders; waiting on confirmation of customer-impacted list before sending.
dinesh: filing incident ticket INC-2026-1749304567 with timeline, evidence S3 path, rotated key id, and action items.
oncall-sre: thumbs up. please ping #incident-ops when evidence collection is complete so we can close containment.
alice: followups (post-mortem owners): ben-platform (for logs + detection rules), dinesh (key rotation + secrets hygiene), alice (process + comms), carol (customer outreach if needed).
carol-cs: marking this thread resolved for now — continuing in incident tracker. :white_check_mark:
